samples.summary: The mixed-key branch of `styleOffAsClear` (one style object containing both a style-supplied key and a non-supplied key) is never exercised, though the test comment claims it is
samples.evidence: In 'keeps an explicit false where the named style supplies the flag' (document.test.ts:345-367) the comment at line 360 says "A key the style does not supply is still cleared **in the same write**", but the test issues two *separate* `applyInlineStyle` calls: `{ italic: false }` then `{ bold: false }`. The interesting branch in `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:405-417) is the copy-on-write path `cleared = cleared ?? { ...style }` combined with `if (defaults[key]) continue`, i.e. a single patch like `{ italic: false, bold: false }` on a Heading 6 where `italic:false` must survive while `bold` is deleted. A regression that built `cleared` as `{}` instead of a spread of `style`, or that cleared/kept the wrong key when both are present, would drop the italic override and no test in the diff or elsewhere would fail. I grepped packages/docs/test for combined boolean-off patches and found none.

samples.summary: The `applyInlineStyleToCells` (cell-rectangle) copy of the new `styleOffAsClear` call has no test for the toggle-off clearing
samples.evidence: document.ts:431 adds `styleOffAsClear` to the cell-rectangle write path, but the updated view assertions in backward-selection-toggle.test.ts (lines 475, 579, 635, 717) all go through `Doc.applyInlineStyle` / `visitRangeSlices` (their surrounding describes are titled 'cell endpoints normalize to the parent table' and set anchor/focus inside cells, not a `tableCellRange`). I grepped packages/docs/test for `tableCellRange` (5 files: table-merge-context, backward-selection-toggle, cell-range-expand, editor-read-only, editor-step-selection-font-size) and found no assertion that a boolean turned off via a cell-rectangle selection ends with the key absent — only font-size/read-only concerns. So if the second call site were left un-wrapped, no test would fail.

samples.summary: The new `mergeInlineStyle` key-deletion behavior for `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` (non-boolean keys like color/fontSize) is asserted only with `toBeFalsy()`, which passes under both the old and the new representation
samples.evidence: block-helpers.ts now deletes keys whose patch value is `undefined` instead of leaving a phantom `key: undefined` entry, and its doc comment names `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` as the primary consumer. The only CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE tests (document.test.ts:161-211) assert `expect(after.color).toBeFalsy()` etc., and their comment at lines 180-184 still describes the *old* `{ ...inline.style, ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE }` spread and explicitly says it is "tolerant of either representation". So the phantom-key removal for color/fontSize/etc. is untested (only the boolean path asserts `'italic' in style === false`), and the stale comment now misdescribes the code.

samples.summary: The per-document style override input to `styleOffAsClear` (`this._document.styles`) is never exercised by a test
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` resolves defaults via `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), this._document.styles)` (document.ts:410), so a document-level override that *adds* a boolean to a style (toggle-off must keep explicit `false`) or that *removes* Heading 6's built-in italic (toggle-off must clear the key) both change the outcome. All new tests use built-in styles only (Heading 6 / paragraph). I grepped packages/docs/test for `styles:` overrides feeding `Doc` and found override coverage only in named-styles.test.ts, which tests `resolveStyleInline` in isolation, not the toggle path.

samples.summary: No test asserts that clearing one boolean leaves the run's other explicit styles intact
samples.evidence: `mergeInlineStyle` deletes only patch keys whose value is `undefined`; a regression that deleted more (or dropped `base` keys) would be caught by nothing here. The new tests all operate on runs carrying a single style key ('restores a single run…', 'clears the key for every boolean toggle…'), so e.g. a bold+italic run with italic toggled off (bold must stay `true`, run must not merge with unstyled neighbours) is uncovered.

finding.summary: The mixed-key branch of `styleOffAsClear` (one style object containing both a style-supplied key and a non-supplied key) is never exercised, though the test comment claims it is
finding.evidence: In 'keeps an explicit false where the named style supplies the flag' (document.test.ts:345-367) the comment at line 360 says "A key the style does not supply is still cleared **in the same write**", but the test issues two *separate* `applyInlineStyle` calls: `{ italic: false }` then `{ bold: false }`. A regression that built `cleared` as `{}` instead of a spread of `style`, or that cleared/kept the wrong key when both are present, would drop the italic override and no test in the diff or elsewhere would fail. verdict.reason: The mixed-key branch of styleOffAsClear (document.ts:405-417, specifically `cleared = cleared ?? { ...style }` combined with `if (defaults[key]) continue`) requires a single patch carrying both a style-supplied and a non-supplied boolean-off key. No such test exists. The Heading 6 test at document.test.ts:345-367 issues two separate applyInlineStyle calls ({italic:false} then {bold:false}) while its comment at line 360 claims the clearing happens "in the same write"; with single-key patches `{...style}` and `{}` yield identical results, so the copy-on-write spread is untested and a regression to `{}` (or to keeping/clearing the wrong key when both are present) would pass. I checked every applyInlineStyle call site in every test file repo-wide (document.test.ts, table.test.ts, block-helpers.test.ts, pending-style*.test.ts, backward-selection-toggle.test.ts, table-link.test.ts, editor-read-only.test.ts): all patches are single-key or true-valued. A repo-wide regex for a boolean style key set to false alongside another key found only text-box-editor.test.ts:918, which sets a pre-existing run style on a mounted block and is read via getRangeStyleSummary — it never passes through Doc.applyInlineStyle/styleOffAsClear. Indirect routes were followed too: pending-style.ts:34 could flush a multi-key patch, but pending-style-integration.test.ts:86-93 only stages {bold:true, italic:true} and pending-style.test.ts mocks applyInlineStyle; CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE (types.ts:241-255) is all undefined so it never enters the `style[key] !== false` branch; frontend tests (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1299-1306) call store.applyStyle below this logic. No counterexample found.
